study.title: EU Survey on ICT Usage and e-Commerce in Enterprises 2025: AI module (Model Questionnaire, Module E)
study.citation: Eurostat. (2025, December 17). European businesses statistics compilers' manual for ICT usage and e-commerce in enterprises, 2025 survey (2025 edition; Manuals and guidelines, KS-01-25-065). Publications Office of the European Union. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-manuals-and-guidelines/w/ks-01-25-065
study.sourceLabel: KS-01-25-065, Annex 1 – Model questionnaire (ICT-ENT 2025 V1.5), Module E "Artificial Intelligence" (Eurostat)
study.abstract: This study contains only Module E (Artificial Intelligence) of the Eurostat model questionnaire for the 2025 EU survey on ICT usage and e-commerce in enterprises, as printed in the 2025 compilers' manual; national statistical institutes adapt it for their own surveys. The enterprise reports which AI technologies it uses, for which business purposes, and how it acquired the AI software or systems. Enterprises not using AI are asked whether they ever considered it and, if so, why they do not use it (for example costs, lack of expertise, data protection concerns or unclear legal consequences).
study.universe: Enterprises with 10 or more employees and self-employed persons (NACE Rev. 2 sections C–J, L–N and group 95.1; optional: 0–9). Module E: enterprises with access to the internet.

survey.name: module_e
survey.label: Module E: Artificial Intelligence
survey.hint: (Scope: enterprises with access to the internet, i.e. if A1>0)

survey.name: e_intro
e1
survey.label: Does your enterprise use any of the following Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies?
survey.hint: E1 a) to h) = “No” then go to E4 (if optional included) else go to F1.

survey.name: e1_a
survey.label: a) AI technologies performing analysis of written language (e.g. text mining)
survey.hint: Text mining refers to the use of advanced techniques for automated detection of patterns in (large) texts.

survey.name: e1_b
survey.label: b) AI Technologies converting spoken language into machine-readable format (speech recognition)
survey.hint: Speech recognition is the ability of a machine or program to identify words and phrases in spoken language and convert them to a machine-readable format.

survey.name: e1_c
survey.label: c) AI Technologies generating written or spoken language (natural language generation, speech synthesis)
survey.hint: Natural language generation is the ability for a computer program to convert data into natural language representation.

survey.name: e1_d
survey.label: d) AI Technologies generating pictures, videos, sound/audio

survey.name: e1_e
survey.label: e) AI Technologies identifying objects or persons based on images or videos (image recognition, image processing)

survey.name: e1_f
survey.label: f) Machine learning (e.g. deep learning) for data analysis
survey.hint: Machine learning (e.g. deep learning) involves ‘training’ a computer model to better perform an automated task, e.g. pattern recognition.

survey.name: e1_g
survey.label: g) AI Technologies automating different workflows or assisting in decision making (e.g. AI based software robotic process automation)
survey.hint: Artificial Intelligence based robotic process automation refers to software that automates business processes (e.g. workflows automation) based on Artificial Intelligence technologies.

survey.name: e1_h
survey.label: h) AI Technologies enabling physical movement of machines via autonomous decisions based on observation of surroundings (autonomous robots, self-driving vehicles, autonomous drones)

survey.name: e2
survey.label: Does your enterprise use Artificial Intelligence software or systems for any of the following purposes?

survey.name: e2_a
survey.label: a) Use of AI for marketing or sales
survey.hint:
some of the examples may be:
• customer profiling, price optimisation, personalised marketing offers, market analysis based on machine learning
• chatbots based on natural language processing for customer support
• autonomous robots for orders processing

survey.name: e2_b
survey.label: b) Use of AI for production or service processes
survey.hint:
some of the examples may be:
• predictive maintenance or process optimization based on machine learning
• tools to classify products or find defects in products based on computer vision
• autonomous drones for production surveillance, security or inspection tasks
• assembly works performed by autonomous robots

survey.name: e2_c
survey.label: c) Use of AI for organisation of business administration processes or management
survey.hint:
some of the examples may be:
• business virtual assistants based on machine learning and/or natural language processing, e.g. for document drafting
• data analysis or strategic decision making based on machine learning, e.g. risk assessment based on machine learning
• planning or business forecasting based on machine learning
• human resources management based on machine learning or natural language processing, e.g. candidates pre-selection screening, employee profiling or performance analysis

survey.name: e2_d
survey.label: d) Use of AI for logistics
survey.hint:
some of the examples may be:
• autonomous robots for pick-and-pack solutions in warehouses for parcel shipping, tracing, distribution or sorting
• route optimization based on machine learning

survey.name: e2_e
survey.label: e) Use of AI for ICT security
survey.hint:
some of the examples may be:
• face recognition based on computer vision for authentication of ICT users
• detection and prevention of cyber-attacks based on machine learning

survey.name: e2_f
survey.label: f) Use of AI for accounting, controlling or finance management
survey.hint:
some of the examples may be:
• machine learning to analyse data that helps to make financial decisions
• invoice processing based on machine learning
• machine learning or natural language processing used for bookkeeping tasks

survey.name: e2_g
survey.label: g) Use of AI for research and development (R&D) or innovation activity (excluding research on AI)
survey.hint:
some of the examples may be:
• analysis of data for conducting research, solving research problems, developing a new or significantly improved product/service based on machine learning

survey.name: e3
survey.label: How did you enterprise acquire the Artificial Intelligence software or systems that it uses?

survey.name: e3_a
survey.label: a) They were developed by own employees (including those employed in parent or affiliate enterprise)

survey.name: e3_b
survey.label: b) Commercial software or systems were modified by own employees (including those employed in parent or affiliate enterprise)

survey.name: e3_c
survey.label: c) Open-source software or systems were modified by own employees (including those employed in parent or affiliate enterprise)

survey.name: e3_d
survey.label: d) Commercial software or systems ready to use were purchased (including examples where it was already incorporated in a purchased item or system)

survey.name: e3_e
survey.label: e) External providers were contracted to develop or modify them

survey.name: e4
survey.label: Has your enterprise ever considered using any of the Artificial Intelligence technologies listed in question E1?
survey.hint:
Questions E4 is presented only to respondents who answered ‘No’ to E1a)-h) i.e. enterprises that did not use any of the Artificial Intelligence technologies listed in question E1.
– Optional
(Filter question)

survey.name: e5
survey.label: What are the reasons for your enterprise not to use any of the Artificial Intelligence technologies listed in question E1?

survey.name: e5_a
survey.label: a) The costs seem too high

survey.name: e5_b
survey.label: b) There is a lack of relevant expertise in the enterprise

survey.name: e5_c
survey.label: c) Incompatibility with existing equipment, software or systems

survey.name: e5_d
survey.label: d) Difficulties with availability or quality of the necessary data

survey.name: e5_e
survey.label: e) Concerns regarding violation of data protection and privacy

survey.name: e5_f
survey.label: f) Lack of clarity about the legal consequences (e.g. liability in case of damage caused by the use of Artificial Intelligence)

survey.name: e5_g
survey.label: g) Ethical considerations

survey.name: e5_h
survey.label: h) Artificial Intelligence technologies are not useful for the enterprise
